title.en: Follow the argument line by line
title.es: Seguir el hilo de un argumento

es: Distinguir tesis, evidencia, objeción y réplica en un debate escuchado y ordenarlas en un esquema.

teaching.en: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.
teaching.es: Planteo la tesis de que el tráfico debería quedar fuera del centro los domingos, y nuestra encuesta puede darle más peso.
teaching.explanationEs: Put forward a claim = plantear una tesis; lend weight to = reforzar una idea con datos.
segments: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the
centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.
teaching.audioText: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.

teaching.en: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.
teaching.es: A primera vista, una encuesta a veinte amigos parece una prueba sólida; solo una muestra representativa habla por todo un pueblo.
teaching.explanationEs: On the face of it introduce una apariencia que luego se corrige; la evidencia debe ser comprobable y amplia.
segments: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks
like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.
teaching.audioText: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.

teaching.en: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.
teaching.es: En mi opinión la calle es más agradable sin autos, pero una opinión por sí sola no es evidencia, por firmemente que se sostenga.
teaching.explanationEs: La evidencia se puede comprobar; la opinión solo se puede compartir. No las mezcles en tu argumento.
segments: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion
on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.

teaching.en: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.
teaching.es: Un comerciante puede plantear una objeción: las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos; la réplica es que un autobús gratuito las llevaría.
teaching.explanationEs: La objeción es el argumento contrario; la réplica (rebuttal) responde a esa objeción con un dato o una solución.
segments: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far;
the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.
teaching.audioText: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.

teaching.en: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.
teaching.es: Las cifras que respaldan una tesis pesan poco si la fuente está oculta, porque nadie puede comprobar de dónde proceden.
teaching.explanationEs: Support = respaldar. Una cifra sin fuente no se puede verificar, por eso no funciona como evidencia.
segments: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source
is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.
teaching.audioText: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.

teaching.en: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.
teaching.es: Haz primero un esquema: tu tesis, pruebas sólidas, la objeción más probable y una réplica que pueda poner esta en duda.
teaching.explanationEs: Un esquema (outline) ordena las cuatro piezas; cast doubt on = poner en duda, sin necesidad de demostrar lo contrario.
segments: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest
objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.
teaching.audioText: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.

prompt.es: Localiza la evidencia: ¿qué parte de este texto se puede comprobar?

choices.text: The bus system looks out of date and should be replaced soon.
The town needs more routes so that every resident feels part of public life.
A third of residents miss evening events as the last bus leaves early.

feedback.es: La evidencia es el dato verificable de la encuesta de transporte; lo demás son opiniones sobre lo que «debería» hacerse.

hint.es: La evidencia se puede comprobar; la opinión suele empezar por I feel u Honestly.

origin.text: I feel that the town needs more bus routes. A transport survey found that one in three residents now skips evening events because the last bus stops at eight. Honestly, the whole system looks out of date to me.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las cifras de la encuesta respaldan la tesis de que más gente va en bicicleta.»

feedback.es: Figures support a claim cuando aportan datos que la refuerzan; back o bear out también encajan.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «respaldar»; empieza por s.

origin.text: The survey figures ___ the claim that more people now cycle to work, since fewer cars crossed the bridge this spring.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una objeción es que el puente es demasiado estrecho.»

answer.text: One objection is that the bridge is too narrow

feedback.es: La objeción presenta el argumento contrario con One objection is that…, seguida de una frase completa.

hint.es: Empieza por One objection y sigue con that.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde la hablante a la objeción de los padres.

choices.text: By proposing that clubs meet during the lunch break.
By showing that teenagers sleep better before an early morning match.
By admitting that sport matters more than morning tests ever do.

feedback.es: La réplica a la objeción de los padres es trasladar los clubes a la hora de la comida; el resto no se dice.

origin.audio: Our claim is simple: schools should start at nine. The evidence comes from a sleep study of six hundred teenagers, who did better in morning tests after a later start. Some parents raise an objection, saying that later finishes would disrupt sport. The rebuttal is that clubs can move to the lunch break, when every pupil is free.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la pieza del argumento que representa.

pairs: A survey of nine hundred parents found that most prefer later starts
I honestly feel that mornings are simply too early
Our claim is that the school day should start later
One objection is that parents would finish work earlier
The rebuttal is that clubs could meet at the lunch break

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un papel distinto: el dato comprobable es evidencia, la sensación personal es opinión, y tesis, objeción y réplica ocupan su lugar.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace la hablante con la afirmación del municipio?

choices.text: She backs it while asking for a longer trial period.
She casts doubt on it by noting that its evidence is too thin.
She rebuts it with a new survey of the library's users.
She accepts it but objects to Monday as the closing day.

feedback.es: Señala que un solo mes no es una muestra representativa: pone en duda la afirmación sin aportar datos propios ni aceptarla.

origin.text: The council claims that closing the library on Mondays will save money. The figures it published, however, cover only one month, and they ignore the cost of extra staff elsewhere. A single month is hardly a representative sample, so the claim remains weak.

prompt.es: Escucha el debate y elige qué objeción plantea Leo a la tesis de Sara.

choices.text: That the survey asked too few pupils in too few of the schools.
That pupils who sleep badly need less homework all week.
That weekend homework builds good habits, as he has seen in his family.
That Sara's claim came from an opinion rather than evidence.

feedback.es: Leo basa su objeción en los buenos hábitos que, según él, enseña la tarea de fin de semana; la crítica a la muestra o a la opinión es de Sara, no suya.

origin.audio: At the youth council, Sara opened by putting forward a claim: schools should stop setting homework at weekends. Her evidence came from a survey of eight hundred pupils, most of whom said they slept badly on Sunday nights. Leo raised an objection. In his opinion, weekend homework teaches good habits, and he had seen it work for his cousins. Sara answered that a story about cousins is not hard evidence, and that her sample was representative because it covered twelve schools. Leo conceded that the survey was larger than anything he could offer, but he still wanted some kind of weekly task.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere Sara al responder sobre los primos de Leo?

choices.text: That his cousins are less able than the pupils in the survey.
That weekend homework could not possibly suit any pupil.
That Leo should have surveyed his cousins' school himself.
That a personal story cannot replace evidence from a wide sample.

feedback.es: Sara dice que una historia sobre primos no es evidencia sólida y defiende su muestra amplia: sugiere que una anécdota no sustituye a los datos.

origin.audio: At the youth council, Sara opened by putting forward a claim: schools should stop setting homework at weekends. Her evidence came from a survey of eight hundred pupils, most of whom said they slept badly on Sunday nights. Leo raised an objection. In his opinion, weekend homework teaches good habits, and he had seen it work for his cousins. Sara answered that a story about cousins is not hard evidence, and that her sample was representative because it covered twelve schools. Leo conceded that the survey was larger than anything he could offer, but he still wanted some kind of weekly task.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una sola reseña es una anécdota, no una prueba sólida.»

feedback.es: Hard evidence es la colocación para pruebas sólidas y comprobables; una anécdota aislada no lo es.

origin.text: A single excellent review is an anecdote, not hard ___. It cannot stand for the thousands of customers who never wrote one.

prompt.es: Escribe la tesis y la evidencia de este debate sobre los museos.

answer.text: My claim is that museums should be free. According to a survey, seventy-two per cent of visitors would return more often if entry cost nothing.
accepted: My claim is that museums should be free. According to a survey, seventy-two per cent of visitors would return more often if entry cost nothing.
I am arguing that museums should be free of charge. The survey found that 72 per cent of visitors would come back more often if there were no entry fee.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta separa la tesis (My claim is that…) de la evidencia con su fuente (According to…) y su dato.

origin.text: Debate: ¿deben los museos ser gratuitos? Tu tesis: sí. Tu evidencia: según una encuesta, el 72 % de los visitantes volvería más a menudo si la entrada no costara nada.

evidenceGroups: museums should be free of charge

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere Tom con su réplica sobre quienes dudan de la encuesta?

choices.text: That anyone who doubts it must now produce evidence of their own.
That agreement with earlier surveys makes the small sample irrelevant.
That people who doubt it are acting in bad faith and should be ignored.
That he will run a larger survey next year to settle the matter.

feedback.es: Tom admite la limitación de la muestra y sugiere que quien duda debe aportar sus propias pruebas; no dice que el tamaño sea irrelevante, ni acusa de mala fe, ni anuncia otra encuesta.

origin.text: Tom's rebuttal was brief. He admitted that the survey had reached only two hundred people, but pointed out that its results matched every earlier survey in the region, which would be strange if they were an accident. He did not claim certainty; he suggested only that those who doubted the figures should now produce evidence of their own.

prompt.es: Completa: «Eso puede poner en duda la tesis, aunque no la destruye.»

feedback.es: Cast doubt on es la colocación para poner en duda una afirmación; throw doubt on es una variante menos frecuente.

origin.text: The figures in the report cover only one week. That alone may ___ doubt on the claim, although it does not ruin it.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante de la réplica de los organizadores.

choices.text: It answers the concern so well that no further checks are needed.
It answers the concern, but she wants facts about the noise.
It is reasonable, although she doubts that the market would close at two.
It is a fair reply, but she thinks the organisers should pay for noise monitors.

feedback.es: La hablante acepta la réplica como respuesta al problema, pero pide pruebas sobre el ruido antes de la votación; no dice que sobren las comprobaciones ni duda del horario ni reclama que paguen los organizadores.

origin.audio: Some neighbours object that a Sunday market would be noisy. The organisers reply that it would close at two, long before the evening. I think that answer deals with the worry, though I would still like some hard evidence about the noise before the council votes.
